reading: Every horizontal bar shifts one cell left (a cell pushed past the left edge is lost), then every background 0 becomes 5.
why: output(y,x) = input(y,x+1) if that is non-zero, else 5; offset (0,-1) and map 0->5 are the same on every pair
invariants: bar colours and lengths (except clipping at the left edge)

reading: Each full-width coloured stripe spreads its colour up and down over the 7-rows to the nearest stripe; rows equidistant from two differently coloured stripes become solid 1. The 8 column turns 1 and the 1 crossings on stripe rows turn 8, stripe rows turn 1.

slots.stripes: full rows of one colour c crossed by the vertical line (1 at the crossing)
slots.fill: each plain row takes the colour of its nearest stripe row; ties between different colours -> whole row 1
slots.line: vertical 8 line -> 1 in filled rows; stripe rows -> all 1 with 8 at the crossing

why: every non-stripe row in the output is uniform nearest-stripe colour except the line column (1), or an all-1 tie row

reading: There are objects of two colours, each colour with one repeated shape. Every object of colour A is replaced by the colour-B shape (top-left of bounding box aligned) and vice versa: the two shapes swap.

slots.shapeA, shapeB: the single shape every object of that colour has
slots.place: each A object's box is cleared and shapeB in colour B drawn at its top-left; same for B

why: after swapping, every object position holds the other colour's shape and nothing else changes

reading: Each isolated marker moves by an offset fixed by its colour: 7 up 2, 9 down 2, 2 left 2, 1 right 1.

slots.target: a per-colour offset table learned from training: 7->(-2,0), 9->(+2,0), 2->(0,-2), 1->(0,+1)

why: every marker of colour c appears translated by offset(c); the offset is not one constant, it depends on the colour

reading: Each 1 sitting on top of a 5 post drops straight down to the bottom row, replacing the 5 there; its old cell becomes background.
why: every 1 ends on the bottom row in its own column; nothing else changes except the 5 it covers

reading: Group the 2-cells into clusters (2s within 2 cells of each other, chained); inside each cluster's bounding box every non-2 cell becomes 4.

new_rows.name: box2
new_rows.datalog:
two(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), C = 2.
near(A, B, P, Q) :- two(A, B), two(P, Q), DY = P - A, DX = Q - B, DY >= -2, DY <= 2, DX >= -2, DX <= 2.
grp(A, B, P, Q) :- near(A, B, P, Q).
grp(A, B, E, F) :- grp(A, B, P, Q), near(P, Q, E, F).
gy0(A, B, min(P)) :- grp(A, B, P, Q).
gy1(A, B, max(P)) :- grp(A, B, P, Q).
gx0(A, B, min(Q)) :- grp(A, B, P, Q).
gx1(A, B, max(Q)) :- grp(A, B, P, Q).
box2(Y, X) :- gy0(A, B, Y0), gy1(A, B, Y1), gx0(A, B, X0), gx1(A, B, X1), px(Y, X, K), Y >= Y0, Y <= Y1, X >= X0, X <= X1, !two(Y, X).

why: every non-2 cell inside a 2-cluster box becomes 4; all cells outside the boxes are unchanged
invariants: noise cells outside the cluster boxes

reading: Vertical bars of 8 and 2 stand on the bottom row every second column. A new 5 bar is drawn in the next slot (two columns right of the last bar), bottom-aligned, with height = (number of 8 cells) - (number of 2 cells).

slots.height: count of 8 cells minus count of 2 cells

why: the only change is a bottom-aligned 5 column of that height at that column

reading: Around the two-colour shape, every background cell that touches the shape only diagonally (no orthogonal fg neighbour) is painted with the shape's inner (minority) colour.

new_rows.name: diag_halo
new_rows.datalog:
isfg(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
ortho(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), DY = 0.
ortho(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), DX = 0.
diag(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), !ortho(DY, DX).
dtouch(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), diag(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, isfg(Y2, X2).
otouch(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), ortho(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, isfg(Y2, X2).
diag_halo(Y, X) :- dtouch(Y, X), !otouch(Y, X), !isfg(Y, X).

slots.colour: the less frequent foreground colour of the input (2 in pair 0, 1 in pair 1), not a constant

why: the new cells are exactly the background cells diagonally but not orthogonally adjacent to the shape

reading: A rectangle of colour A holds an inner block of colour B. A frame of colour B is drawn around the rectangle, as thick as the inner block's smaller side, but no thicker than the smallest margin to the grid edge.

new_rows.name: halo
new_rows.datalog:
isfg(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
gh(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
gw(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
top(min(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
bot(max(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
lef(min(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
rig(max(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
ocol(C) :- top(T), lef(L), cell(T, L, C).
inn(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), !ocol(C).
it(min(Y)) :- inn(Y, X).
ib(max(Y)) :- inn(Y, X).
il(min(X)) :- inn(Y, X).
ir(max(X)) :- inn(Y, X).
cand(V) :- it(A), ib(B), V = B - A + 1.
cand(V) :- il(A), ir(B), V = B - A + 1.
cand(V) :- top(V).
cand(V) :- lef(V).
cand(V) :- bot(B), gh(G), V = G - B.
cand(V) :- rig(B), gw(G), V = G - B.
thick(min(V)) :- cand(V).
halo(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !isfg(Y, X), top(T), bot(B), lef(L), rig(R), thick(K), Y0 = T - K, Y1 = B + K, X0 = L - K, X1 = R + K, Y >= Y0, Y <= Y1, X >= X0, X <= X1.

slots.colour: the inner block's colour B (varies per pair)
slots.thickness: min(inner block height, inner block width, distance from rectangle to each grid edge); pair 4 is clipped to 2 by the top/left margin

why: the output adds exactly a uniform-thickness ring of colour B around the rectangle's box
invariants: the rectangle and its inner block

reading: Each 8 object is three cells of a 2x2 square; the missing fourth cell becomes 1.

new_rows.name: nook
new_rows.datalog:
isfg(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
ortho(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), DY = 0.
ortho(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), DX = 0.
diag(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), !ortho(DY, DX).
nook(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !isfg(Y, X), diag(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, isfg(Y2, X2), isfg(Y2, X), isfg(Y, X2).

why: the only changed cells are background cells that complete a 2x2 block with three 8 cells; they become 1
